verdict.rationale: The docs show some least-privilege controls that apply to agents. The AI assistant can be restricted to read-only access [31]. The remote MCP server separates read-only tools from read-write ones [38, 63]. Shares can grant read access to specific users or roles and limit which tables and views are exposed [10, 11, 47]. However, nothing documents actually issuing a dedicated, scoped API credential or token for an agent; the only credential evidence is saving credentials locally [20]. Missing for 10: explicit scoped/read-only token issuance, per-token permission scopes, service or agent accounts, token expiry and revocation, independent or hands-on corroboration.
